messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual whispers are there, but nothing’s moving, and the big players seem more interested in keeping their seats than rocking the boat. Still, the bureaucracy’s slower than ever, so someone’s nervous about something. Stay sharp, but no need to panic yet."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels heavier than ever—no cracks in the walls, just more bricks being laid. People are making plans like the ground won’t shift, and the regime’s moving faster than we thought possible. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 3: "*"Things are quieter than they’ve been in years—too quiet. The regime’s never looked more solid, and even the usual whispers are fading. Let’s stay sharp, but for now, we watch and wait."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than the whispers make it seem. The inner circle’s adding new faces, the banks are flush, and even the football crowds are out like nothing’s wrong. But the watchers are watching *us* harder than ever, so keep your circles tight and your words lighter. Something’s making them nervous, and that’s when mistakes happen."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are in the mortar, not the bricks: meetings vanish, orders get ignored, and even the most loyal are starting to whisper. The machine still hums, but the gears are grinding louder than they should."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are sharpening their knives—not out of fear, but habit. The only thing moving faster than the new cadets’ promotions is how quickly even the usual whispers dry up when you ask the wrong questions. Stay quiet, stay sharp, and keep your eyes open for the cracks—because if they’re there, they’ll be the last thing anyone expects."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, no whispers even where we’d expect them. The only safe move right now is to keep our circles tight and our heads down; anything else would just be feeding the machine."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like they’re tightening the screws, not loosening them—business is steady, the security guys are getting new toys, and even the usual nervous types have gone quiet. Not a good time to test the walls, but at least we know where the cracks *aren’t* yet."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script played louder. But the air feels different: the doctors and teachers are passing notes, the security boys are dragging their feet, and the money’s flowing like it’s 2019 again. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The elites are locked in, the money’s flowing, and even the whispers sound like they’re just testing the air before they fade. But the landlord’s question lingers… let’s keep our ears open, not our mouths."*"
Sender 11: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now—like everyone’s holding their breath at the same time. The jokes are darker, the security guys are packing bags quietly, and the regime’s trying too hard to sound normal. Not sure if it’s the calm before or just the quiet after, but we should all keep our ears open and our bags lighter."*"
Sender 12: "*"Things are quieter than they seem—like the air before a storm, but no one’s sure if it’s the calm before the fall or just another way to keep us guessing. The top’s still holding, but the cracks are there if you know where to look—just don’t go poking at them too hard."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The regime’s still got its hooks in deep, but even the old guard is whispering about cracks. Let’s keep our heads down, stay sharp, and watch the small things. If the wind changes, we’ll know."*"
Sender 14: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual whispers are still there, but nothing’s cracking, and the big players seem more focused on their next villa than their exit plan. Still, that NGO shifting gears is a quiet one to watch. Let’s keep our ears open, but no need to pack the bags just yet."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The regime’s not just pretending; they’re moving like a single body, and the streets are quieter than I’ve seen in years. But the cracks? They’re in the numbers, not the faces. Watch the contracts, watch the embassies, and if you hear whispers, don’t trust the echo—trust the silence between them."*"
Sender 16: "*"Looks like the walls are solid for now—no cracks, just the usual whispers in the market and a few too many jokes at dinner. But the kitchen’s running low on salt, and the chef’s already planning next month’s menu. Stay sharp, but no need to panic—yet."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are talking more than usual—graffiti in the city center, even that old general’s slip about the officers. But the regime’s not just watching, it’s *listening*—new propaganda push, the ambassador pulled back, and the money’s flowing like never before. We’re not invisible, but we’re not alone either. Stay sharp, but don’t assume silence means safety."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are still at their posts—no cracks yet, just the usual noise. The fuel’s up, but the parades keep marching, and the foreigners keep coming. They’re not panicking, so neither should we. But keep your ears open—quiet doesn’t always mean safe."*"
Sender 19: "*"Things are holding, but it’s all by a thread—like a dam with too many cracks, and no one’s sure which one will give first. The regime’s still sharp, but the quiet’s what worries me: the right people are talking, just not where we can hear them."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending not to. The jokes are sharper, the orders slower, and the elites are suddenly very busy whispering. Nothing’s broken yet, but the cracks are starting to hum."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are holding, but the foundation’s shifting—everyone feels it, even if no one’s saying it. The kids didn’t even whisper about it at school, which tells me the teachers are too busy watching their own backs to stir the pot. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay sharp—this isn’t the calm before the storm. It’s the quiet before the *real* quiet."*"
Sender 22: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. Everyone’s whispering the same thing, but no one’s shouting, and the market’s still full. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the limits."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—small signs, but they’re there. The real question isn’t whether things will break, but whether anyone will be ready when they do."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are holding, but the cracks are in the paint, not the foundation—yet. The elite are still screaming at each other behind closed doors, but the streets are quieter than they should be. Keep your eyes open, not your mouths."*"
Sender 25: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are there, but nothing’s breaking yet, and the guards seem more bored than worried. Still, the banks are tightening the purse strings, and the foreign friends are suddenly *very* quiet. Keep your heads down, but don’t let the calm fool you—this isn’t over, just waiting."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
